steps.q: Does it make a great product or service?

views.text: In July 2025, Equity Mates described Duolingo’s app as interactive and sticky, offering 40+ languages, and said it was expanding into other subjects like maths, music, chess and literacy to broaden its education product.

steps.q: Will it keep earning above market profits?

views.text: In March 2026, a guest on Equity Mates said Duolingo held about 85% of language-learning daily active users and, at that scale, captured billions of exercises each day to train its own models, framing data and scale as its edge.

views.text: In July 2025, Equity Mates outlined a bull case that AI could power learning of anything on a platform with proven user engagement, suggesting Duolingo’s user experience and AI could help it capture more of education.

steps.q: Can it reinvest its profits productively?

views.text: In March 2026, Equity Mates reported management intentionally traded off this year’s financial metrics for a larger long term goal, prioritising user acquisition over extracting more from current users after a narrative shift around AI and competition.

steps.q: Can it be bought at a reasonable price?

views.text: In March 2026, Equity Mates said Duolingo was at one of its lowest valuations, citing a P/E of 12, forward P/E of 15, a prior average of 150, PEG around 0.6 to 0.8, and about a billion dollars cash with zero debt, and noted the market priced in slower growth.
